name: optimize-claim-batch
prompt: We run this Lua script on Dragonfly v1.34.0 via EVALSHA: dragonfly-scripting-workbench/dragonfly-scripting-workspace/evals/inputs/claim_mailbox_batch.lua (its KEYS/ARGV contract and how to seed realistic data are in dragonfly-scripting-workbench/dragonfly-scripting-workspace/evals/inputs/claim_mailbox_batch_CONTRACT.md). Production calls it with candidate_window=1024, batch_size=32 against a due zset of about 1000 mailboxes with ~2 KB records, all keys under the hashtag {inbound}; the server runs with --proactor_threads=4 --cache_mode=false --maxmemory=2048Mi and no other flags. It feels slow. Optimize it without changing its reply protocol or its recovery semantics. Deliver: the optimized .lua file, a short NOTES.md explaining every change and why it is safe, and before/after numbers measured on a local Dragonfly of the same version (docker image docker.dragonflydb.io/dragonflydb/dragonfly@sha256:366e34f415c22983dc1c4a1d575fa2d9c22b9a3998a9934bf1cc6d16c17695db is already pulled; you may start containers named eval-*; tear them down when done). Do not modify anything outside your output directory except throwaway containers.
expected_output: Optimized script with identical replies on identical seeded state; per-candidate HGET loops replaced by chunked HMGET; whole-window protocol checks preserved; measured before/after with the execution-path counters or SCRIPT LATENCY; no Redis-only advice.
assertions: reply-equality-with-original: the optimized script returns replies byte-identical to the original on the same seeded state, proven by running scripts/bench_script.py --compare (clock-bearing reply positions excluded)
p50-improved-on-same-seed: the measured p50 of the optimized script is lower than the original's p50 measured on the same seed and the same container
per-candidate-hget-loop-batched: the per-candidate HGET/HMGET-per-mailbox loop over the candidate window is replaced by batched multi-field reads
before-after-numbers-present: the deliverables contain concrete before/after numbers measured against a Dragonfly v1.34.0 container, not estimates
reply-protocol-and-recovery-preserved: the whole-window protocol/version checks and the lease-receipt recovery semantics are unchanged

states-execution-regime-with-evidence: the notes state that this script is io-coordinated on the given default flags because a shared hashtag does not co-locate keys on one shard without --lock_on_hashtags, and support that statement with the eval_io_coordination_total / eval_shardlocal_coordination_total deltas per invocation or an equivalent measurement taken on the v1.34.0 container

before-after-on-identical-seeded-state: the before/after comparison is run on identical seeded state (the seed re-applied before each timed call) with a reply-equality check between the two variants, and both p50 and p99 are reported for each arm

no-unverified-redis-only-advice: every performance claim in the output cites Dragonfly-specific evidence -- a Dragonfly execution-path counter (eval_io_coordination_total / eval_shardlocal_coordination_total / lua_blocked_total), a SCRIPT LATENCY or bench measurement taken on v1.34.0, or a Dragonfly v1.34.0 doc/source citation -- and the output contains no Redis-origin performance advice presented without such Dragonfly evidence
